title: Implement a responsive invoices admin page with sorting, filters and bulk actions from a Figma file
prompt:
Implement the Ledgerline invoices page from our Figma file as a real, responsive admin page. The Figma file is design.json (Figma REST API format). Its page holds two top-level frames, Desktop (1280 wide) and Mobile (390 wide); every node has a descriptive name, an absoluteBoundingBox, fills, strokes, corner radii, effects and, for text, the characters and style. desktop.png and mobile.png are the two frames rendered. Match both frames closely (sizes, spacing, colors, radii, borders, shadows, Inter typography) and use every string and number exactly. Build one responsive page: the Desktop frame from 768px up and the Mobile frame below 768px, using real responsive CSS (flexbox or grid plus media queries), not absolutely positioned boxes. Between 768px and 1280px the desktop layout must adapt without horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text. Use semantic HTML: aside and nav for the sidebar, header, main, a real table with thead and th header buttons for the invoices on desktop, and a list of invoice cards on mobile, both rendered from one invoice data array. On mobile the sidebar collapses into the menu button, the KPI cards form a 2x2 grid, the status tabs become a Status select next to a Sort select, and the table becomes cards.

Make it work:
- Sorting (desktop): Issued, newest first, is the default. Clicking Client, Issued, Due date or Amount sorts by that column and shows an arrow on the active header; a second click reverses the order. Amount sorts high to low first (Halcyon Health $18,600.00 first, Mosaic Coffee $860.00 last); Client sorts A to Z first.
- Status tabs All, Paid, Pending, Overdue and Draft filter the rows and show live counts. The 'Filter by client…' box narrows the rows by client name (case-insensitive) together with the active tab.
- Selection: every row has a checkbox and the header checkbox selects or clears all visible rows. While any row is selected, a bulk bar replaces the tabs row with 'N selected', a 'Mark as paid' button and a 'Clear' button. Mark as paid sets the selected invoices to Paid, then recalculates the tab counts and the KPI cards: Outstanding = total of Pending and Overdue invoices (note: 'N open invoices'), Overdue = total of Overdue invoices, Collected in September = total of Paid invoices.
- Mobile: the menu button opens a slide-in drawer with the sidebar navigation (Invoices active) that closes with its close button or Escape. The Status select (All statuses, Paid, Pending, Overdue, Draft) filters the cards and the Sort select offers Newest first, Oldest first, Amount: high to low and Amount: low to high.
interaction_hints: Desktop: click the Amount header once (Halcyon Health first) and again (Mosaic Coffee first); click Client (Brightline Studio first). Click the Overdue tab (only INV-2045 and INV-2042), then All; type north in the client filter. Tick the INV-2045 and INV-2042 checkboxes, check the bulk bar reads 2 selected, click Mark as paid and read the tab counts (Paid 6, Overdue 0) and KPI cards (Outstanding $11,485.75, Overdue $0.00, Collected in September $54,455.75). Tick the header checkbox (10 selected). Mobile: open the menu drawer and close it with Escape; choose Overdue in the Status select (2 cards) and Amount: high to low in the Sort select (Halcyon Health first). For mobile checks run the interaction helper with --width 390 --height 844; for the intermediate-width check use --width 1024 --height 768 and eval document.documentElement.scrollWidth (must be at most 1024).

rubric.criterion: At 1280px the page matches the Desktop frame: white sidebar (Ledgerline logo, Menu items with Invoices active and its 10 badge, Workspace items, Pro plan card, Nora Alvarez row), top bar with the search field and ⌘K hint, breadcrumb, 'Invoices' title and subtitle, Export CSV and New invoice buttons, four KPI cards, and the table card with status tabs, client filter, ten rows and the 'Showing 10 of 10 invoices' footer with pagination, at matching positions and sizes.

At 390px the page matches the Mobile frame: app bar with menu button, logo, bell and avatar (no sidebar), stacked title block, Export and New invoice side by side, KPI cards in a 2x2 grid with the shortened labels and notes (e.g. 'Collected (Sep)', 'Oldest 12 days'), Status and Sort selects side by side, a full-width client filter, and ten invoice cards (client tile, name, 'INV-… · Issued …', amount, divider, due date, status pill) instead of a table.

Visual style matches: Inter, royal blue #2451d6 for the primary button, active tab and active nav item, colored client initial tiles, status pills with dots (green Paid, amber Pending, red Overdue, gray Draft), red due dates on overdue invoices, about 12px card radii, light borders and soft shadows.

All data matches exactly: KPI values $21,746.50, $10,260.75, $44,195.00 and 14.6 days with their notes, and all ten invoices with number, client, email, issued date, due date, amount and status (e.g. INV-2045, Northwind Traders, finance@northwind.co, Sep 9, 2026, Sep 23, 2026, $7,920.00, Overdue).

Reading the source: one page with media queries and flex/grid layout (not absolutely positioned boxes), aside/nav, header and main landmarks, a real table with thead and th for the desktop invoices, and the mobile cards rendered from the same data as the table.

Sorting works: the first click on Amount puts Halcyon Health ($18,600.00) first and Mosaic Coffee ($860.00) last, a second click reverses it, Client sorts Brightline Studio first and Tidal Wave Media last, and the active header shows a direction arrow.

Filtering works: the Overdue tab shows exactly INV-2045 and INV-2042 and becomes the active tab, Paid shows 4 rows, All restores 10, and typing 'north' in the client filter leaves only Northwind Traders.

Bulk action works: selecting INV-2045 and INV-2042 shows a bar with '2 selected' and Mark as paid; clicking it turns both to Paid, the tabs read Paid 6 and Overdue 0, and the KPI cards read Outstanding $11,485.75 (3 open invoices), Overdue $0.00 and Collected in September $54,455.75.
The header checkbox selects every visible row ('10 selected' on All, '2 selected' on the Overdue tab) and clears them again; Clear deselects all and restores the tabs row.
At 390px the menu button opens a drawer with the sidebar navigation (Invoices marked active) that closes with its close button and with Escape.
At 390px the Status select set to Overdue leaves exactly two invoice cards, and the Sort select set to Amount: high to low puts Halcyon Health first and Mosaic Coffee last.
At 1024x768 there is no horizontal page scrolling and no overlapping or clipped text (the table may scroll inside its own container), and nothing overflows at 390px.

title: Implement a responsive profile settings page with validation, dirty state and a theme switch from a Figma file
prompt:
Implement the Northstar profile settings page from our Figma file as a real, responsive web page. The Figma file is design.json (Figma REST API format). Its page holds two top-level frames, Desktop (1280 wide) and Mobile (390 wide); every node has a descriptive name, an absoluteBoundingBox, fills, strokes, corner radii, effects and, for text, the characters and style. desktop.png and mobile.png are the two frames rendered. Match both frames closely (Roboto, colors, radii, borders, shadows, spacing) and use every string exactly. Build one responsive page: the Desktop frame from 768px up and the Mobile frame below 768px, using real responsive CSS (flexbox or grid plus media queries), not absolutely positioned boxes. Between 768px and 1280px the desktop layout must adapt without horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text. Build it as one semantic form: nav for the top navigation and for the settings sections, main, a section with a heading per card, a label for every control, real text and email inputs, selects, a textarea, radio groups in fieldsets with legends for Date format and Theme, and the four switches as checkbox inputs or role='switch' buttons. On mobile the header becomes a back-button app bar, the settings sections become a tab strip that scrolls horizontally inside itself, fields stack in one column, the theme cards shrink to three compact cards and Discard / Save changes sit in a bar fixed to the bottom of the viewport.

Behavior:
- Save changes starts disabled (the muted violet in the design). Any edit (text, select, radio, switch, theme) enables it; Discard restores every control to the design values and disables it again. Clicking an enabled Save changes shows a 'Settings saved' toast for about three seconds, replaces 'Last saved Sep 22, 2026 at 4:18 PM' with 'All changes saved' and disables the button until the next edit.
- The bio counter shows the live length as 'N / 160' (94 / 160 initially); the textarea accepts at most 160 characters and the counter turns red at 160.
- Email: on blur, a value that is not a valid address (for example 'maya@') shows 'Enter a valid email address' in red under the field, gives the field a red border and hides the Verified badge; Save changes stays disabled while an error is shown, and fixing the value clears the error.
- Date format updates the example line: MM/DD/YYYY gives 'Example: 09/24/2026', DD/MM/YYYY gives 'Example: 24/09/2026', YYYY-MM-DD gives 'Example: 2026-09-24'.
- Theme: choosing Dark selects that card and immediately switches the whole page to a dark palette (dark page and card backgrounds, light text); Light switches back; System follows prefers-color-scheme.
- The settings section links (desktop list and mobile tabs) mark the chosen item active; sections other than Profile may show a short placeholder panel with the section title.
interaction_hints: Type in First name and check that Save changes becomes enabled, then click Discard and confirm the value and the disabled state return. Change the email to maya@, press Tab, and look for the red message and border; restore it. Type into the bio and read the counter; paste 200 characters and confirm it stops at 160 in red. Pick DD/MM/YYYY and YYYY-MM-DD and read the example line. Pick Dark and screenshot, then Light. Toggle Product updates and click Save changes: look for the toast and 'All changes saved'. Read the HTML for labels, fieldsets and switch semantics. For mobile checks run the interaction helper with --width 390 --height 844; for the intermediate-width check use --width 1024 --height 768 and eval document.documentElement.scrollWidth (must be at most 1024).

rubric.criterion: At 1280px the page matches the Desktop frame: top nav (Northstar logo, five links with Settings underlined, search, bell, avatar), title and subtitle, the settings list with Profile active and the Need a hand? card, the Profile card (avatar, Upload photo, Remove, two-column fields, bio with hint and counter), the Preferences card (language, date format radios with example, three theme cards) and the Email notifications card with four switches, then the action bar with Last saved, Discard and Save changes.

At 390px the page matches the Mobile frame: back-button app bar with centered 'Settings' and avatar, the section tab strip with Profile underlined (cut off at the right edge), single-column fields, date format radios stacked, three compact theme cards in a row, switches with wrapped descriptions, the centered Last saved line and the bottom bar with Discard and Save changes side by side.

Visual style matches: Roboto, violet #6d28d9 for the active nav underline, active settings item, radios, switches and selected theme card (2px violet border on a lavender fill), a green Verified pill inside the email field, white cards with 12px radius and light borders, 8px inputs, and the muted (disabled) Save changes button.

Text matches exactly: every label, value and description, the bio 'Designing calm, accessible tools for research teams. Previously at Fieldwork and Lumen Health.' with '94 / 160', the four notification titles and descriptions, and 'Last saved Sep 22, 2026 at 4:18 PM'.

Reading the source: one page with media queries and flex/grid layout, a form whose controls all have associated labels, real email/text inputs, selects and a textarea, radio groups inside fieldsets with legends, and switches implemented as checkboxes or role='switch' with aria-checked.
Dirty state works: Save changes is disabled on load, editing any field enables it, and Discard restores all original values (including switches, date format and theme) and disables it again.

Email validation works: entering 'maya@' and leaving the field shows 'Enter a valid email address' with a red border and hides Verified, Save changes stays disabled while the error shows, and correcting the address clears the error.
The bio counter updates live ('N / 160'), input stops at 160 characters, and the counter turns red at 160.
Date format radios update the example to 'Example: 24/09/2026' for DD/MM/YYYY and 'Example: 2026-09-24' for YYYY-MM-DD, and back to 'Example: 09/24/2026'.
Choosing the Dark theme card selects it and switches the page to a dark palette with readable light text; choosing Light restores the light design.
After an edit, Save changes shows a 'Settings saved' toast, the footer line changes to 'All changes saved', and the button is disabled again.

At 390px the section tab strip scrolls horizontally inside itself without page overflow and the Discard / Save changes bar stays fixed to the bottom of the viewport while scrolling; at 1024px wide there is no horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text.

title: Implement a responsive product listing with combined filters and sorting from a Figma file
prompt:
Implement the Fernhill Outdoor backpacks listing from our Figma file as a real, responsive storefront page. The Figma file is design.json (Figma REST API format). Its page holds two top-level frames, Desktop (1280 wide) and Mobile (390 wide); every node has a descriptive name, an absoluteBoundingBox, fills, strokes, corner radii, effects and, for text, the characters and style. desktop.png and mobile.png are the two frames rendered. Match both frames closely (Open Sans, colors, radii, spacing, shadows) and use every string and price exactly. Draw each backpack illustration with CSS shapes or inline SVG, matching the design's shapes and colors (no images). Build one responsive page: the Desktop frame from 768px up and the Mobile frame below 768px, using real responsive CSS (flexbox or grid plus media queries), not absolutely positioned boxes. Between 768px and 1280px the desktop layout must adapt without horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text. Use semantic HTML: header with nav, a breadcrumb nav, an aside holding a filter form (fieldsets with real checkboxes, capacity chips as toggle buttons or checkboxes, number inputs for the price range, color swatches as buttons with accessible names, rating radios and an In stock only switch), a real select for sorting, and the products as a list of article cards whose icon buttons have accessible labels. On mobile the sidebar is replaced by Filters and Sort buttons above a two-column grid.

Product data (Featured order is the design order): Daypacks are Ridgeline, Canyon, Metro and Sprint; Hiking packs are Summit, Trailhead and Alpine; Travel packs are Voyager and Nomad. Colors: Forest is Ridgeline and Alpine, Sand is Canyon and Nomad, Slate is Metro, Rust is Summit and Sprint, Navy is Trailhead, Black is Voyager. Capacity comes from the name. Metro costs $59 (was $79) and Nomad is sold out.

Behavior:
- Filters combine with OR inside a group (two categories show both) and AND across groups. Capacity chips: Under 20L (below 20), 20–35L, 36–50L, 50L+ (above 50). The price inputs filter by current price, inclusive. A swatch toggles its color. Rating: 4.5 & up or 4.0 & up. In stock only hides sold-out products.
- The result text reads 'Showing N products' ('Showing 1 product' for one) and the mobile count 'N products' updates too. When nothing matches, show 'No backpacks match these filters' with a 'Clear all filters' button. 'Clear all' resets every filter.
- Sort by offers Featured, Price: low to high, Price: high to low and Top rated (ties keep Featured order), applied on top of the filters.
- Heart buttons toggle a filled saved state; the dark plus buttons add the product to the cart and increment the badge from 2.
- Mobile: Filters opens a full-screen sheet with the same filter groups, a close button and a sticky footer button 'Show N products' whose N updates live; tapping it closes the sheet. Sort opens the same sort options.
interaction_hints: Tick Hiking packs (expect Summit 45L Hiking Pack, Trailhead 35L, Alpine 55L Expedition and 'Showing 3 products'), add Travel packs (5), then clear. Tick Daypacks and the 20–35L chip (only Ridgeline and Canyon). Set the max price to 150 (Ridgeline, Canyon, Metro, Trailhead, Sprint). Click the Rust swatch alone (Summit, Sprint). Toggle In stock only (8). Tick Travel packs + Under 20L for the empty state and use Clear all filters. Choose Price: low to high and read the order. Click two plus buttons (badge 4) and a heart. Mobile: open Filters, tick Hiking packs, read 'Show 3 products', tap it and count the cards. For mobile checks run the interaction helper with --width 390 --height 844; for the intermediate-width check use --width 1024 --height 768 and eval document.documentElement.scrollWidth (must be at most 1024).

rubric.criterion: At 1280px the page matches the Desktop frame: dark green promo bar, header (Fernhill logo, six nav links with Packs & Bags underlined and Sale in orange, search, account, saved and cart icons with badge 2), breadcrumb, 'Backpacks' title and intro, the filter sidebar (Category, Capacity chips, Price inputs and range, Color swatches, Rating, In stock only) with Clear all, 'Showing 9 products' with the Sort by select, a 3x3 product grid, and the viewed-9-of-9 progress with Back to top.

At 390px the page matches the Mobile frame: short promo bar, header with menu button, centered logo, search and cart, breadcrumb, title with '9 products', the Filters and 'Sort: Featured' pill buttons, a two-column product grid with smaller tiles and single-line names, and the progress line; no sidebar.

The nine backpack illustrations are recognizable versions of the design's drawings in matching colors on matching tinted tiles: daypack with front pocket and handle loop, roll-top with buckle strap, hiking packs with lid and hip belt (sleeping pad or bottle), commuter with reflective strip, travel packs with framed front panel and side handle, and the running vest with two flasks.

Text matches exactly: the nine names, capacity and color lines, star ratings with review counts, prices including $59 in orange with $79 struck through, the New, Best seller, −25% and Sold out badges, filter labels with counts (4), (3), (2), and the promo, breadcrumb and intro copy.

Reading the source: one page with media queries and grid/flex layout, header/nav, an aside with a form of fieldsets and real inputs, a select for sorting, product cards as a list of articles, icon buttons with aria-labels, and illustrations built from CSS or inline SVG (no raster images).

Combined filters work: Hiking packs alone shows exactly Summit 45L Hiking Pack, Trailhead 35L and Alpine 55L Expedition with 'Showing 3 products'; adding Travel packs shows 5; Daypacks plus 20–35L shows only Ridgeline 28L Daypack and Canyon Roll-Top 22L.
A max price of 150 shows exactly Ridgeline, Canyon, Metro, Trailhead and Sprint; the Rust swatch alone shows Summit and Sprint; In stock only hides Nomad and shows 8 products.

Sorting works on top of filters: Price: low to high orders Metro, Sprint, Canyon, Ridgeline, Trailhead, Nomad, Summit, Voyager, Alpine; Price: high to low reverses it; Top rated starts Alpine (4.9), Summit (4.8); an active filter stays applied after sorting.
Travel packs plus Under 20L shows 'No backpacks match these filters' with a Clear all filters button that restores all nine products and 'Showing 9 products'.
Clicking the plus button on two products raises the cart badge from 2 to 4, and a heart button toggles a filled saved state on and off.

At 390px, Filters opens a full-screen sheet with the filter groups and a 'Show N products' button whose number updates live (3 after ticking Hiking packs); tapping it closes the sheet and the grid shows those 3 products.
At 1024x768 the sidebar and product grid fit without horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text, and nothing overflows at 390px.

title: Implement a responsive onboarding wizard step with live slug generation and validation from a Figma file
prompt:
Implement step 2 of the Plotline onboarding wizard from our Figma file as a real, responsive, working flow. The Figma file is design.json (Figma REST API format). Its page holds two top-level frames, Desktop (1280 wide) and Mobile (390 wide); every node has a descriptive name, an absoluteBoundingBox, fills, strokes, corner radii, effects and, for text, the characters and style. desktop.png and mobile.png are the two frames rendered. Match both frames closely (Lato, the navy progress panel, coral accents, radii, the focus ring, spacing) and use every string exactly. Build one responsive page: the Desktop frame from 768px up and the Mobile frame below 768px, using real responsive CSS (flexbox or grid plus media queries), not absolutely positioned boxes. Between 768px and 1280px the desktop layout must adapt without horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text. Use semantic HTML: an aside with an ordered list for the stepper, main with a form, a label for every control, radio inputs for team size and checkboxes for the use-case cards (styled as the chips and cards in the design). On mobile the side panel and testimonial disappear, an app bar shows a back button and 'Step 2 of 4' above a four-segment progress bar, team-size chips form a 2x2 grid, use-case cards stack, and Back / Continue sit in a bar fixed to the bottom of the viewport.

Behavior:
- The workspace URL follows the name live until the user edits the URL field directly: lowercase, spaces and underscores become single hyphens, other characters are removed, no leading or trailing hyphens (typing 'Blue Harbor Studio!' gives 'blue-harbor-studio').
- URL status (right of the field on desktop, under it on mobile): '✓ Available' in green for a valid slug, 'Use at least 3 characters' for shorter slugs, and 'That URL is taken' in red for plotline, admin or acme. Only lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens are accepted.
- Team size is single-select; use-case cards are multi-select and toggle their coral check.
- Continue validates: an empty name shows 'Enter a workspace name' under the field, an invalid or taken URL keeps its message, and no selected use case shows 'Pick at least one use case'. The page stays on step 2 and focus moves to the first invalid field. Enter in a text field acts like Continue.
- A valid Continue shows step 3 in the same page: title 'Invite your teammates', three email inputs with the placeholder 'name@acmedesign.co', an 'Add another' link (up to 5 rows), 'Skip for now' and a 'Send invites' button. The stepper marks step 2 done with a check and makes step 3 current, the eyebrow reads 'STEP 3 OF 4', and on mobile three progress segments are filled and the app bar reads 'Step 3 of 4'.
- Back on step 3 returns to step 2 with every value preserved.
interaction_hints: Clear the workspace name and type Blue Harbor Studio! (URL should become blue-harbor-studio with ✓ Available). Set the URL to ab, then to admin, and read the status. Clear the name and click Continue (message, focus on the name field, still step 2). Unselect Product roadmaps and click Continue ('Pick at least one use case'). Fill valid values and click Continue: step 3 with 'Invite your teammates', stepper step 2 checked, eyebrow STEP 3 OF 4; click Add another until five rows; click Back and confirm the values. Repeat Continue at 390px and read the progress bar and 'Step 3 of 4'. For mobile checks run the interaction helper with --width 390 --height 844; for the intermediate-width check use --width 1024 --height 768 and eval document.documentElement.scrollWidth (must be at most 1024).

rubric.criterion: At 1280px the page matches the Desktop frame: the navy panel (Plotline logo, two-line heading, subheading, four-step vertical stepper with done, current and upcoming states and connectors, testimonial card with stars, quote, avatar, name and role) and the white form area (Having trouble? Contact support, STEP 2 OF 4 eyebrow, title, body, focused name field, URL field with the plotline.app/ prefix and ✓ Available, hint, four team-size chips with 11–50 selected, three use-case cards with Product roadmaps selected, auto-join checkbox, divider, Back and Continue).

At 390px the page matches the Mobile frame: app bar with back chevron, logo and 'Step 2 of 4', four progress segments (two filled), 'Next: Invite your teammates', title and body, stacked fields with ✓ Available under the URL field, 2x2 team-size chips, three full-width use-case cards with icon, text and check circle, the wrapped auto-join checkbox, and the bottom bar with Back and a wide Continue.

Visual style matches: Lato, navy #1b1f3b panel with soft glow circles, coral #f0643c for the logo, eyebrow, focus ring, selected chip and card, checks and Continue (with its coral shadow), green Available text, 10-12px radii, and tinted icon tiles on the use-case cards.

Text matches exactly: step titles and descriptions, the quote and 'Dana Whitfield, Head of Operations, Brightside', 'Set up your workspace' copy, 'Acme Design Co', 'acme-design-co', the hint, chip labels, use-case titles and descriptions, and the auto-join sentence.

Reading the source: one page with media queries and flex/grid layout, an ordered list stepper, a form with labels, radio inputs for team size and checkbox inputs for use cases, and state kept in script rather than separate hard-coded pages.
Slug generation works: typing 'Blue Harbor Studio!' as the name sets the URL to 'blue-harbor-studio' live, and after the URL is edited by hand, name changes no longer overwrite it.
URL status works: 'ab' shows 'Use at least 3 characters', 'admin' shows 'That URL is taken' in red, and a valid slug shows '✓ Available' in green.
Team size behaves as a single choice, use-case cards toggle independently, and Continue with no use case selected shows 'Pick at least one use case'.

Continue validates and advances: an empty name shows 'Enter a workspace name', stays on step 2 and focuses the field; valid data shows step 3 ('Invite your teammates', three email inputs, Send invites) with step 2 checked and step 3 current in the stepper, the eyebrow 'STEP 3 OF 4', and at 390px three filled segments with 'Step 3 of 4'.
On step 3, Add another adds email rows up to five, and Back returns to step 2 with the name, URL, team size and use cases preserved.
Pressing Enter in the workspace name field acts like Continue (validation or advance).
The Back / Continue bar stays fixed to the bottom of the 390x844 viewport while scrolling, and at 1024x768 there is no horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text.

title: Implement a responsive dark analytics dashboard with a working date-range switch from a Figma file
prompt:
Implement the Tideline Analytics overview from our Figma file as a real, responsive dashboard. The Figma file is design.json (Figma REST API format). Its page holds two top-level frames, Desktop (1280 wide) and Mobile (390 wide); every node has a descriptive name, an absoluteBoundingBox, fills, strokes, corner radii, effects and, for text, the characters and style. desktop.png and mobile.png are the two frames rendered. Match both frames closely (dark palette, Inter, teal accents, radii, borders) and use every label and number exactly. Draw the visitors chart, KPI sparklines, share bar and country bars with HTML/CSS or inline SVG from data, not images: the 30 daily bars must have the design's relative heights (read them from the 'Bar / Sep N' nodes), weekend days in the darker slate color, and Sep 24 highlighted with its tooltip. Build one responsive page: the Desktop frame from 768px up and the Mobile frame below 768px, using real responsive CSS (flexbox or grid plus media queries), not absolutely positioned boxes. Between 768px and 1280px the desktop layout must adapt without horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text. Use semantic HTML: header with nav, main, section cards with headings, a real table for Top pages on desktop and a list on mobile. On mobile the nav collapses into a menu button, the range switch spans the width, KPI cards form a 2x2 grid without sparklines and the cards stack.

Behavior:
- The 7D / 30D / 90D / 12M switch is a button group (aria-pressed) that updates the subtitle date range, the four KPI values and deltas, the comparison note and the chart:
  7D: Sep 24 – Sep 30, 2026; Visitors 11,382 ▲ 4.2%; Sessions 16,905 ▲ 3.6%; Conversion rate 3.71% ▲ 0.2 pts; Revenue $20,918 ▲ 6.3%; 7 daily bars (the last seven days of the design data) labeled Thu 24 … Wed 30; note 'vs prev. 7 days'.
  30D: the design (Sep 1 – Sep 30, 2026, 'vs prev. 30 days').
  90D: Jul 3 – Sep 30, 2026; Visitors 139,870 ▲ 9.7%; Sessions 207,115 ▲ 7.2%; Conversion rate 3.55% ▼ 0.1 pts; Revenue $241,760 ▲ 11.4%; 13 weekly bars; note 'vs prev. 90 days'.
  12M: Oct 1, 2025 – Sep 30, 2026; Visitors 512,904 ▲ 31.8%; Sessions 768,331 ▲ 27.5%; Conversion rate 3.48% ▲ 0.6 pts; Revenue $902,115 ▲ 42.0%; 12 monthly bars labeled Oct … Sep; note 'vs prev. 12 months'.
  Rising values use the green pill with ▲ and falling values the red pill with ▼.
- Hovering or focusing any chart bar moves the tooltip above it with that bar's date and value (in 30D, Sep 24 reads 'Thu, Sep 24' and '2,418 visitors'; the 30 daily values sum to 48,210).
- Top pages sorts by clicking the Views, Visitors, Avg. time or Bounce rate headers (numbers compared numerically, times as seconds). The first click sorts high to low, except Bounce rate, which sorts low to high first; a second click reverses; the active header shows ↓ or ↑. Default: Views, high to low.
- Mobile: the menu button opens a drawer with the five nav items, and a sort select above the Top pages list offers the same sorts.
interaction_hints: Click 90D and read the KPI values, subtitle, note and count the bars (13); click 7D (7 bars labeled Thu 24 to Wed 30, Visitors 11,382); click 30D to restore. Hover the Sep 24 bar and another bar and read the tooltip. Click the Bounce rate header (/docs/getting-started first, / last) and the Avg. time header (/docs/getting-started 5m 46s first, / 1m 05s last). Mobile: open the menu drawer, switch ranges and use the Top pages sort select. For mobile checks run the interaction helper with --width 390 --height 844; for the intermediate-width check use --width 1024 --height 768 and eval document.documentElement.scrollWidth (must be at most 1024).

rubric.criterion: At 1280px the page matches the Desktop frame: top bar (Tideline logo, five nav tabs with Overview active, tideline.io switcher, bell, avatar), Overview title and subtitle, the range switch with 30D active and Export, four KPI cards with delta pills, notes and sparklines, the Visitors chart card beside Traffic sources, and the Top pages table beside Top countries.

At 390px the page matches the Mobile frame: app bar with menu button, logo and avatar, title with two-line subtitle, full-width range switch, KPI cards in a 2x2 grid without sparklines, a full-width chart with four x labels and the tooltip beside the Sep 24 bar, Traffic sources, Top pages as a list (path, bounce and time, views) and Top countries.

title: Design a design-system foundations and component variant sheet as a layered Figma-ready SVG
prompt:
Create the foundations and core components page of Harbor, our design system, as one layered SVG file. The canvas is 1440 by 1800 (viewBox 0 0 1440 1800) with a white background rect. It will be imported into Figma, so organize it like a designer's file: every <g> gets a readable id that becomes its layer name (use ' / ' for hierarchy, never ids like g12), components are nested groups, and all copy stays live <text> (no outlined text). Use plain vectors only: no <image>, foreignObject, <script>, CSS animation or external references. Use Inter for all text. Every rect and group position and size (x, y, width, height and translate offsets) is a multiple of 4, sections start 48px from the left edge, each section has a 24px semibold title, and sections are separated by 64px of empty space.

Top-level groups, in this order: 'Header' (title 'Harbor foundations' at 40 bold and 'v2.0 · Updated Sep 2026'), 'Foundations / Color', 'Foundations / Type', 'Foundations / Spacing', 'Components / Button', 'Components / Input', 'Components / Badge'.
- Color: three ramps, groups 'Color / Primary', 'Color / Neutral' and 'Color / Danger', each with exactly five swatch groups named 'Color / <Ramp> / <step>' for steps 100, 300, 500, 700 and 900. A swatch is a 120 by 72 rect with rx 8 plus two labels under it: the step and its uppercase hex, which must equal the rect's fill. Primary 500 is #1F6FEB and Danger 500 is #D92D20; every ramp gets lighter toward 100 and darker toward 900.
- Type: six groups 'Type / Display', 'Type / H1', 'Type / H2', 'Type / H3', 'Type / Body', 'Type / Caption', each with the sample 'The quick brown fox' at the exact size and weight and a spec label: Display 48/56 Bold, H1 36/44 Bold, H2 28/36 Semibold, H3 20/28 Semibold, Body 16/24 Regular, Caption 12/16 Medium (font-size and font-weight attributes must match the spec).
- Spacing: eight groups 'Space / 4', 'Space / 8', 'Space / 12', 'Space / 16', 'Space / 24', 'Space / 32', 'Space / 48', 'Space / 64', each a Primary 500 bar 16 tall whose width is the token value times 4 (16 to 256), with the token label to its left, all bars left-aligned.
- Button: a 3 by 3 variant grid of groups named 'Button / Variant=<Primary|Secondary|Ghost>, State=<Default|Hover|Disabled>', each 136 by 40 with rx 8 and a centered 'Button' label, 24px gaps, with row and column labels. Hover is visibly darker than Default, Disabled has clearly reduced contrast, Secondary has a 1px border, Ghost has no fill.
- Input: groups 'Input / State=Default', 'Input / State=Focus' (2px Primary 500 border) and 'Input / State=Error' (Danger 500 border plus the helper 'Enter a valid email' in Danger 500), each a 320 by 40 field with the label 'Email' above it and a value or placeholder inside.
- Badge: five pills 'Badge / Neutral', 'Badge / Info', 'Badge / Success', 'Badge / Warning', 'Badge / Danger', 24 tall, fully rounded, 12px medium text with a 6px leading dot, colored by meaning.

rubric.criterion: Reading the SVG source: exactly the seven top-level groups with the ids 'Header', 'Foundations / Color', 'Foundations / Type', 'Foundations / Spacing', 'Components / Button', 'Components / Input' and 'Components / Badge' in that order, with readable nested ids and no anonymous or g12-style ids.
The root viewBox is 0 0 1440 1800, all copy is live <text> in Inter, and there is no <image>, foreignObject or <script>.

Color: three ramp groups with exactly five swatch groups each, named 'Color / <Ramp> / <step>' for 100, 300, 500, 700 and 900; each swatch rect is 120x72 with rx 8, its hex label equals its fill in uppercase, Primary 500 is #1F6FEB, Danger 500 is #D92D20, and lightness decreases from 100 to 900.

Type: six style groups whose samples read 'The quick brown fox' with font-size and font-weight matching 48/700, 36/700, 28/600, 20/600, 16/400 and 12/500, each with its spec label (e.g. 'H2 28/36 Semibold').
Spacing: eight 'Space / N' groups whose bars are 16 tall with widths 16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 192 and 256, left-aligned, in Primary 500, each labeled.

Button: nine groups named exactly 'Button / Variant=…, State=…' covering Primary, Secondary and Ghost by Default, Hover and Disabled; each is 136x40 with rx 8 and a centered 'Button' label, 24px apart; Hover is darker than Default, Disabled is muted, Secondary has a 1px border and Ghost has no fill; row and column labels are present.

Input: three groups 'Input / State=Default', 'Input / State=Focus' and 'Input / State=Error', each 320x40 with the 'Email' label; Focus has a 2px #1F6FEB border and Error a #D92D20 border with 'Enter a valid email'.
Badge: five pill groups (Neutral, Info, Success, Warning, Danger), 24 tall and fully rounded, each with a 6px leading dot and 12px medium label in a color that fits its meaning.

Rect and group geometry uses multiples of 4 (spot-check at least 20 values), sections start 48px from the left with 24px section titles and 64px between sections, and nothing overlaps, is clipped or runs outside the canvas when rendered.
The sheet looks like documentation a professional design team would publish: consistent alignment and spacing, a cohesive palette built from the ramps, and clear typographic hierarchy.

title: Design a landing page at three breakpoints on column grids as a layered Figma-ready SVG
prompt:
Design the landing page of Fieldnote, a note-taking app, at three breakpoints in one layered SVG file. The canvas is 2888 by 2440 (viewBox 0 0 2888 2440) with a #EEF1F4 background rect and three top-level frame groups, each starting with a white background rect of the frame size: 'Desktop / 1440' (1440 by 1400 at x 80, y 120), 'Tablet / 768' (768 by 1720 at x 1600, y 120) and 'Mobile / 360' (360 by 2240 at x 2448, y 120), each with a 14px frame label 24px above it. It will be imported into Figma, so organize it like a designer's file: every <g> gets a readable id that becomes its layer name (use ' / ' for hierarchy, never ids like g12), components are nested groups, and all copy stays live <text> (no outlined text). Use plain vectors only: no <image>, foreignObject, <script>, CSS animation or external references. Use Inter, brand #0F766E, text #0B1B1A.

Column grids: Desktop 12 columns of 86 with 72 margins and 24 gutters; Tablet 8 columns of 65 with 40 margins and 24 gutters; Mobile 4 columns of 70 with 16 margins and 16 gutters. Each frame's second child is a group 'Layout grid' holding exactly its column rects (full frame height, fill #FF3B30, opacity 0.06). Content edges must sit on column edges.

Each frame then has these groups in order: 'Nav', 'Hero', 'Features', 'Testimonial', 'Footer'.
- Nav: Desktop shows the logo, links Product, Templates, Pricing and Blog, 'Log in' and a 'Get Fieldnote' button; Tablet shows the logo, 'Get Fieldnote' and a menu icon; Mobile shows the logo and a menu icon.
- Hero: the headline 'Notes that organize themselves' (Desktop 64/72, Tablet 48/56, Mobile 36/44, bold), a subheadline, a primary 'Get Fieldnote free' and a secondary 'See how it works' button, and a vector product mockup group 'Mockup' (app window with sidebar, note list and an open note). Desktop: copy on columns 1 to 6, mockup on columns 7 to 12. Tablet: copy across all 8 columns above the mockup. Mobile: stacked, both buttons full width (328).
- Features: a section title and three card groups 'Card / Capture anywhere', 'Card / Auto-tagging', 'Card / Search everything' (icon, title, two-line text). Desktop: three across, each 4 columns wide (416). Tablet: two cards 4 columns wide (332) on the first row and the third 8 columns wide (688) below. Mobile: stacked, 328 wide.
- Testimonial: the quote 'Fieldnote replaced three apps for our research team.' with an avatar, 'Maya Chen' and 'Head of Research, Lumen'.
- Footer: logo, three link columns on Desktop and Tablet stacked into one column on Mobile, and '© 2026 Fieldnote, Inc.'.
Copy must be identical across the three frames.

rubric.criterion: Reading the SVG source: three top-level frame groups 'Desktop / 1440', 'Tablet / 768' and 'Mobile / 360' whose first child is a white rect of 1440x1400, 768x1720 and 360x2240 at x 80, 1600 and 2448 (y 120), each with a label above and the child groups 'Layout grid', 'Nav', 'Hero', 'Features', 'Testimonial', 'Footer' in order.
The root viewBox is 0 0 2888 2440, all copy is live <text> in Inter, and there is no <image>, foreignObject or <script>.
Each 'Layout grid' holds exactly 12, 8 and 4 column rects with widths 86, 65 and 70, starting at the 72, 40 and 16 margins with 24, 24 and 16 gutters, at full frame height with opacity about 0.06.

Content snaps to the grids: on Desktop the hero copy ends by column 6 and the mockup spans columns 7 to 12; feature cards are 416 wide on Desktop, 332 + 332 then 688 on Tablet, and 328 on Mobile, with their left edges on column edges.
Nav adapts: Desktop has four links, Log in and Get Fieldnote; Tablet has the logo, Get Fieldnote and a menu icon; Mobile has the logo and a menu icon.
Type scale: the headline is 64, 48 and 36 bold on Desktop, Tablet and Mobile, and the Mobile buttons are full width (328).
Copy is identical and complete in all frames: the headline, both button labels, the three feature titles, the quote with 'Maya Chen' and 'Head of Research, Lumen', and '© 2026 Fieldnote, Inc.'.
The 'Mockup' group is a convincing vector app window (window bar, sidebar, note list and open note) at every breakpoint.
Nothing overlaps, is clipped or runs outside its frame; vertical spacing between sections uses multiples of 8 and is consistent within each frame.
All three breakpoints look like a polished, modern SaaS landing page a professional designer would hand off: clear hierarchy, cohesive teal palette, and balanced white space.

title: Design a 24px icon set with navigation component variants built from reusable symbols as a Figma-ready SVG
prompt:
Create the icon set and navigation components of Orbit, our product UI kit, as one layered SVG file. The canvas is 1200 by 1000 (viewBox 0 0 1200 1000) with a white background rect. It will be imported into Figma, so organize it like a designer's file: every <g> gets a readable id that becomes its layer name (use ' / ' for hierarchy, never ids like g12), components are nested groups, and all copy stays live <text> (no outlined text). Use plain vectors only: no <image>, foreignObject, <script>, CSS animation or external references. Use Inter for labels, brand #6941C6 and neutral #1D2939.

Icons: define 16 icons once in <defs> as <symbol> elements with ids icon-home, icon-search, icon-bell, icon-calendar, icon-chat, icon-user, icon-settings, icon-heart, icon-star, icon-folder, icon-camera, icon-lock, icon-trash, icon-download, icon-plus and icon-close, each with viewBox 0 0 24 24. Draw them on a 24px grid with a 2px safe margin (all geometry inside 2 to 22), using only strokes: stroke='currentColor', stroke-width 2, stroke-linecap round, stroke-linejoin round and fill none on every shape. Every icon must be instantly recognizable and share one visual weight.

Top-level groups, in this order:
- 'Icons': a section title plus an 8 by 2 grid of groups 'Icon / <Name>' (Home, Search, Bell, Calendar, Chat, User, Settings, Heart, Star, Folder, Camera, Lock, Trash, Download, Plus, Close), each a 96 by 112 cell with a <use> of its symbol at 48 by 48 in #1D2939 and the name in 12px below.
- 'Tab bar': three variants 'Tab bar / Active=Home', 'Tab bar / Active=Chat', 'Tab bar / Active=Profile', each 375 by 84 with four tab groups Home, Search, Chat and Profile (icon-user), 24px icons via <use> above 11px labels; the active tab is #6941C6 with a 4px indicator bar, the others #667085.
- 'Sidebar item': four variants 'Sidebar item / State=Default', 'State=Hover', 'State=Active' and 'State=Disabled', each 240 by 40 with rx 8, a 20px calendar icon via <use>, the label 'Calendar' and a count badge '3'; Hover gets a light gray fill, Active a #F4EBFF fill with brand icon and label, Disabled 40% opacity.
- 'Icon button': six variants named 'Icon button / Size=<32|40|48>, Style=<Filled|Outline>' showing icon-plus at 16, 20 and 24; Filled is brand with a white icon, Outline has a 1px #D0D5DD border and a #1D2939 icon; all fully rounded.
No icon path data may be duplicated outside <defs>: every icon on the page is a <use>.

rubric.criterion: Reading the SVG source: <defs> contains exactly the sixteen <symbol> elements with the listed ids (icon-home … icon-close), each with viewBox 0 0 24 24.

Icon construction rules hold in every symbol: shapes use stroke='currentColor', stroke-width 2, round linecaps and linejoins and fill none, and all coordinates stay within the 2 to 22 live area (spot-check at least six symbols).
The root viewBox is 0 0 1200 1000, labels are live <text> in Inter, there is no <image>, foreignObject or <script>, and every icon outside <defs> is a <use> (no duplicated icon paths).
'Icons' has sixteen 'Icon / <Name>' groups in an 8x2 grid of 96x112 cells, each using its matching symbol at 48x48 in #1D2939 with its name below.

The sixteen icons are each instantly recognizable as their name (home, magnifier, bell, calendar, speech bubble, person, gear, heart, star, folder, camera, padlock, trash can, download arrow, plus, close X) and share one consistent visual weight and style.

'Tab bar' has three 375x84 variants named 'Tab bar / Active=Home', 'Active=Chat' and 'Active=Profile', each with Home, Search, Chat and Profile tabs; only the named tab is #6941C6 with a 4px indicator and the rest are #667085.

'Sidebar item' has four 240x40 rx 8 variants (Default, Hover, Active, Disabled) with the calendar icon, 'Calendar' and a '3' badge, and the states are styled as specified (gray hover fill, #F4EBFF active fill with brand icon and label, 40% opacity disabled).

'Icon button' has six variants named 'Icon button / Size=…, Style=…' at 32, 40 and 48 with plus icons at 16, 20 and 24, Filled in brand with a white icon and Outline with a 1px #D0D5DD border, all fully rounded.
Sections are aligned on a clear grid with consistent spacing, variants line up in rows, and nothing overlaps, is clipped or runs outside the canvas when rendered.
The sheet looks like a professional UI-kit page: crisp icons with optical balance, consistent component styling and a cohesive purple and neutral palette.
